claims.text: Equimolar WTaTiVZr has greater plastic strain and toughness than pure tungsten at high temperature.
High-entropy alloying stabilizes a homogeneous, fine-grained microstructure in WTaTiVZr.
The stabilized microstructure has enhanced grain-boundary cohesion.
Local lattice distortions in WTaTiVZr promote activation of multiple slip systems at high temperature.
Arc melting followed by repeated homogenization can produce a uniform, equiaxed WTaTiVZr microstructure with minimized residual stresses.
Matching the recrystallized grain size, texture, and thermomechanical history of WTaTiVZr and pure tungsten isolates the effect of multicomponent alloying.
The multiple refractory elements in near-equal proportions create local lattice distortions.
Local lattice distortions broaden the distribution of local stress fields.
The broadened local stress fields increase dislocation nucleation and glide on multiple slip systems.
Multicomponent refractory alloying reinforces grain boundaries against intergranular fracture at high temperature.
Between 1000°C and 1200°C in inert atmosphere, WTaTiVZr will show greater tensile elongation and plastic strain than pure tungsten.
Between 1000°C and 1200°C in inert atmosphere, WTaTiVZr will show greater Charpy impact toughness than pure tungsten.
The proposed mechanism is expected to remain valid up to approximately 1200°C when oxidation and phase instability do not dominate.
Improved macroscopic ductility and toughness should coincide with stronger grain-boundary integrity and measurably different dislocation or slip-system activity relative to pure tungsten.
